name: Pronator Syndrome
definition: Median nerve compression in the proximal forearm, producing aching forearm pain and median-distribution paresthesia without classic nocturnal carpal tunnel pattern.

investigations.principle: Diagnosis is mainly clinical; electrodiagnostics and ultrasound are selective.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, cartilage, tendon, occult injury or other condition-specific assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific diagnostic pathway.

amber: Persistent focal compression with objective deficit may require decompression.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Hasta/Vata-neuropathy phenotype may be documented only in parallel.

patientEducation.summary: Median nerve compression in the proximal forearm, producing aching forearm pain and median-distribution paresthesia without classic nocturnal carpal tunnel pattern.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute neurovascular compromise, major trauma, severe deformity, progressive weakness, suspected tendon rupture, infection or other listed red flags.
